Plot types

Source: R/types.R
kply_register_type.Rd

A type maps a short name ("point", "line", "bar", ...) to the attributes of a plotly.js trace plus defaults. Types live in a registry, so you can add your own with kply_register_type(). The names are those of kggplot.

Usage

kply_register_type(
  name,
  trace,
  params = list(),
  color = c("marker.color", "line.color"),
  sort = FALSE
)

kply_types()

Arguments

name

Name of the type.

trace

Named list of plotly.js trace attributes defining the type, e.g. list(type = "scatter", mode = "lines").

params

Default trace attributes, overridden by the arguments of the call (e.g. list(line = list(width = 1))).

color

Paths of the trace attributes that receive the colour of the series, e.g. c("marker.color", "line.color").

sort

If TRUE, the data are sorted by x before drawing (lines).

Value

kply_register_type() returns name invisibly; kply_types() a character vector of the registered types.

Details

Built-in types: point, line, step, area and bar (alias col).

Examples

kply_types()
#> [1] "point" "line"  "step"  "area"  "bar"   "col"  
kply_register_type(
  "linepoint", list(type = "scatter", mode = "lines+markers"),
  color = c("marker.color", "line.color"), sort = TRUE
)
kplotly(pressure, "temperature", "pressure", type = "linepoint")
